title: CityGML building ground outlines use the stated envelope system
gate: AUD2 3D candidate intake; offline receipt only, no runtime gate claimed
status: offline checks passed; image rebuild and runtime rehearsal required

inputs.crsBasis: EPSG:25832, the horizontal part of the urn:ogc:def:crs,crs:EPSG::25832,crs:EPSG::5783 the file states

inputs.reason: states a coordinate reference system that is not an EPSG code, so its outlines stay unplaced (source srsName: #local-CRS-1)

readerPolicyAndPins.whyChanged: The good original states its system and tuple dimension only on the CityModel's boundedBy/Envelope. The former ancestor-only policy could not carry them to its Building coordinates. The approved envelope-inheritance decision requires changing native_citygml.py, not guessing a system in the converter.
readerPolicyAndPins.change: For srsName and srsDimension, effectiveDeclaration is resolved from the nearest containing feature's own gml:boundedBy/gml:Envelope, unless a nearer literal declaration overrides it. Existing ancestor declarations and nearestAncestorDeclaration, raw literals, numeric values and byte locators remain unchanged. Tuple splitting uses the effective dimension; no dimension default is added.
readerPolicyAndPins.pins: citygmlReaderSha() and the CityGML profile/configuration already hash native_citygml.py, so their content pins change automatically. No pin list or persisted profile was edited. The profile owner must requalify the changed repository bytes before native reads run; pending jobs/readings under the former pins may be stale.
readerPolicyAndPins.otherPins: native_gis.py is also in documentReaderSha's list, so its usual pending-document pin impact applies. The new citygml_outline.py is not independently listed there; any expansion of document pin coverage belongs to that seam's owner.

path: accepted CityGML summary -> existing intake-native-derivative job -> citygml-ground-outline/1 -> content-addressed GeoJSON child with native-derivative/1 lineage -> existing streamed GeoJSON package path -> officer review

invariants.outline: Each Building's own lod0FootPrint wins; otherwise use its GroundSurface polygons at the first source-declared GroundSurface LoD. Never lod0RoofEdge, solid silhouette, or composed BuildingParts. Multiple polygons and interior rings retain their source positions.
invariants.placement: Only literal EPSG systems qualify, through the existing _horizontal_epsg helper. Compound single codes and the GML compound URN use the horizontal part with explicit words. Local, absent and unknown systems stay unplaced. An unusable geometry declaration never falls back to a usable envelope.
invariants.heights: Source z stays in positions. normalize_area keeps it in sourceHeights with unit=null and reference=null; measured height remains unknown, value=null.
invariants.lineage: Properties retain supplied gml:id, basis, LoD and the reader's polygon element/byte locators. Missing ids are not invented. Sidecar positions are Building element ordinals. Original bytes are unchanged; the parent keeps nativeReaderJobId through conversion and replay creates no duplicate child.
invariants.review: Settling the native reading creates no registry record, package or card target directly; it only queues the existing derivative job.

followUp.why: eaf43a25 failed the whole CityGML reading with ENVELOPE_CONFLICT when one feature stated more than one gml:boundedBy/gml:Envelope; before that commit the same file was read, so odd files regressed.
followUp.change: native_citygml.py no longer fails. A feature with more than one envelope supplies no inherited srsName or srsDimension and stops inheritance there, so neither envelope nor an outer one is chosen. The reading records a finding {code: ENVELOPE_CONFLICT, status: needs_input, elements, locators} with the feature's element ordinal and byte span, and its status is partial. citygml_outline.py leaves geometry under that feature without its own declaration unplaced, in words saying the feature states more than one envelope; a sibling building with one envelope is still placed.
followUp.pins: native_citygml.py bytes changed again, so citygmlReaderSha() and the CityGML profile pins change automatically; the profile owner requalifies them with the CG1 bytes. No pin list was edited.
